prerequisites: Mathematical prior knowledge of the fundamentals of differential and integral calculus and linear algebra

learning_outcomes.text: Students master the basics and laws for calculating currents and voltages in electrical DC and AC circuits.
They have the ability to analyze electrical networks, describe them mathematically correctly, and transform them.
They have understood the basics of complex AC circuit calculation and can apply them to practical examples.

syllabus_topics: Linear DC circuits: reference directions; current and voltage sources; Kirchhoff's equations; simple resistor networks (voltage divider, current divider); real current and voltage sources; interactions between source and load (interconnection of voltage sources, power matching, efficiency); superposition principle; analysis of extensive networks.

Transition to time-dependent current and voltage forms: overview and introduction of various characteristic quantities (mean value, rectified value, RMS value, maximum value, peak value, peak-to-peak value, oscillation amplitude).

Alternating current and alternating voltage: phasor diagram; complex AC circuit calculation; description of concentrated RLC components and ideal sources; introduction of locus curves; calculation of simple AC circuits via the complex plane; energy and power in AC voltage; power matching.
Analysis of networks: mesh current method; nodal potential method.

Introduction to two-ports: port condition; two-port equations in matrix form (impedance, admittance, hybrid, chain form); two-port properties (reciprocity, symmetry); matrices of elementary two-ports.
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam.
